nodes.name: Chemical Vapor Transport
nodes.procedure: The mixture of stoichiometric high-purity Ni (nickel powder), P (phosphorus block, red), S (sulfur block) (Ni:P:S = 1:1:2:3), and iodine (10 mg cm⁻³) as transport agents was sealed in an evacuated quartz ampoule and stored in a two-zone furnace (650-600 °C) for 1 week. Large bulk NiPS₃ can be harvested at lower temperature zone.
nodes.source_text: The synthesis of bulk NiPS₃ crystals used the typical chemical vapor transport technology... Large bulk NiPS₃ can be harvested at lower temperature zone.

nodes.name: Electrochemical Exfoliation
nodes.procedure: The electrochemical workstation (Autolab PGSTAT204) was employed to carry out the electrochemical exfoliation under a two-electrode system, with a Pt wire as the counter electrode and bulk NiPS₃ as the working electrode. The electrolyte was prepared by dissolving 0.05 M tetrabutylammonium tetrafluoroborate (TBAB, 98%) in 30 mL N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF, 99.5% Å). During the exfoliation process, a static bias voltage of -5 V was applied to the working electrode, causing the bulk NiPS₃ to expand and peel off, forming a brown suspension. This suspension was then subjected to an ice bath ultrasonic treatment at 300 W power for 90 min to further exfoliate and disperse the NiPS₃ layers. After the ultrasonic treatment, the product was washed with ethanol five times to remove any residual electrolytes or impurities. Finally, the product was vacuum-dried at 60 °C overnight.

nodes.name: In-situ EG Reduction
nodes.procedure: EE-NiPS₃ was used as a substrate for the growth of Ir nanoparticles. Firstly, uniformly disperse 12 mg EE-NiPS₃ in 10 mL ethylene glycol through ultrasound. Later, 420 μL aqueous solution containing 0.1 M K₂IrCl₆ was added to the above suspension and subjected to ultrasonic treatment for 20 min. Then, the flask was placed in the oil bath which was preheated to 120 °C. After fully removing dissolved oxygen, the mixed solution was added to the flask and maintained at 120 °C for 3 h under continuous magnetic stirring and Ar atmosphere. After the product was cooled to room temperature, it was washed with ethanol and deionized water centrifuged multiple times, and dried under vacuum overnight at 60 °C.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-TEM images show uniform size of loaded Ir NPs with average particle size of ~1.94 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy (AC-TEM) and high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images (Fig. 2a–c) clearly show that the size of the loaded Ir NPs is uniform with an average particle size of ~1.94 nm (Fig. 2b, inset).

nodes.characterization_summary: Magnified HAADF-STEM image illustrates crystallinity of Ir NPs with legible lattices; inset shows Ir (111) lattice fringes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The magnified HAADF-STEM image clearly illustrates the crystallinity of Ir NPs with legible lattices (Fig. 2c). By focusing on a single NP, lattice fringes can be observed and ascribed to the Ir (111) crystal plane (Fig. 2c, inset, upper right).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows Ir (111) d-spacing of 0.235 nm and NiPS₃ (130) d-spacing of 0.289 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A more intuitive high-resolution TEM image (Fig. 2d) shows the d-spacing of 0.289 nm (130) of NiPS₃ and 0.235 nm (111) of Ir.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED identifies NiPS₃ (110)/(130)/(131)/(133)/(352) planes and Ir (111) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the selected area electron diffraction pattern (SAED, Fig. 2e), the NiPS₃ (110)/(130)/(131)/(133)/(352) planes and Ir (111) plane can be clearly identified.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of elements in Ir/NiPS₃ heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The successful incorporation of Ir NPs with NiPS₃ was further confirmed by the elemental mapping (Fig. 2f), where the distribution of each element was relatively uniform.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows NiPS₃ (001)/(131)/(202)/(060)/(133) peaks at 14.1°/36.0°/49.5°/54.5°/57.8° with no detectable Ir peaks due to ultrafine NP size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Supplementary Fig. 7 shows the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns... For Ir/NiPS₃ the peaks at 14.1°/36.0°/49.5°/54.5°/57.8° respectively correspond to the (001)/(131)/(202)/(060)/(133) planes of NiPS₃, and no Ir peak was found due to the detection difficulty of ultrafine NPs (<2 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of Ir/NiPS₃ show red shift relative to EE-NiPS₃ due to hindered vibration after Ir loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks of Ir/NiPS₃ heterostructures undergo a red Raman shift relative to EE-NiPS₃. This is attributed to the hindered vibration activity of the NiPS₃ substrate atoms after Ir loading.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows stronger O-H vibration and EG ligand peaks (-CH₂, C-H, C=O) on Ir/NiPS₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the Fourier transform infrared spectra (FT-IR, Supplementary Fig. 9), the Ir/NiPS₃ heterostructure has a stronger interaction with water than NiPS₃, because of the higher O-H vibration intensity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks shift -0.29 eV indicating NiPS₃ electron acceptor role; Ir 4f shows Ir⁴⁺/Ir⁰ ratios of 0.61/1 (Ir NPs) and 0.64/1 (Ir/NiPS₃).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Relative to EE-NiPS₃, the Ni 2p peaks shift about -0.29 eV for Ir/NiPS₃ material (Fig. 3a), indicating the electron acceptor role of NiPS₃ here. Ir 4f spectra of Ir NPs and Ir/NiPS₃ samples were compared in Fig. 3b, showing the co-existence of Ir⁰ and Ir⁴⁺ doublets. The Ir⁴⁺/Ir⁰ ratios were further calculated to 0.61/1 for Ir NPs and 0.64/1 for Ir/NiPS₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows reduction state of Ni; Ir L₃-edge shows increased oxidation state in Ir/NiPS₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3c presents the Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra of Ir/NiPS₃. Compared to EE-NiPS₃, the downshift of XANES edge presents the reduction state of Ni in Ir/NiPS₃... While in the Ir L₃-edge XANES spectra, the higher white line intensity manifests the reduced electronic density and the increased Ir oxidation state in Ir/NiPS₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ni-S/Ni-Ni bond shortening, Ir-Ir bond lengthening, and new Ir-Ni coordination in Ir/NiPS₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The local coordination environment was further studied in Fig. 3e by the Fourier transform function extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra... Compared with EE-NiPS₃, characteristic peaks representing the Ni-S and Ni-Ni coordination shifted significantly to a low R-value in Ir/NiPS₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: DPC-STEM reveals anisotropic electric field around Ir NP with Janus electronic state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The color plot in Fig. 5a shows the non-uniform distribution of the electric field (EF) around a single Ir NP on NiPS₃. The arrow presents the irregular direction of electron transfer around the Ir particle.

nodes.characterization_summary: KPFM shows surface potential ΔEs = 34.2 mV for Ir/NiPS₃ vs 6.9 mV for NiPS₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ir/NiPS₃ sample showed a greater surface potential (ΔEs = 34.2 mV, Fig. 5c, d) compared with pure NiPS₃ (ΔEs = 6.9 mV).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during HER shows H₃O⁺ peak at ~1750 cm⁻¹ and Eg(2) blue shift indicating H spillover.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the applied potential gradually decreases, a Raman peak newly appears at ~1750 cm⁻¹ in Ir/NiPS₃, belonging to the H₃O⁺ intermediate species... the peak of Eg(2) undergoes a blue shift during the HER.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates gives Cdl = 35.92 mF cm⁻² for Ir/NiPS₃, higher than EE-NiPS₃ (17.68 mF cm⁻²) and Ir/C (21.80 mF cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4b displays the higher Cdl and ECSA of Ir/NiPS₃ (35.92 mF cm⁻²) than those of EE NiPS₃ (17.68 mF cm⁻²), Ir/C (21.80 mF cm⁻²), and other samples.
